final_answer:
Let
\[
s_0=\chi(x),\quad s_1=\chi(x-1),\quad s_3=\chi(x-3),\quad s_{-3}=\chi(x+3).
\]
At the four branch points one of these symbols is \(0\), so neither \(A(p)\) nor \(B(p)\) counts those \(x\).

For non-branch \(x\), all four symbols are \(\pm1\). If
\[
Q_p=\sum_x\chi\bigl(x(x-1)(x-3)(x+3)\bigr),
\]
then
\[
A+B=\frac{p-4+Q_p}{2}.
\]

Now compute the pairwise second moment
\[
E=\sum_{\substack{x\in\mathbb F_p\\x\notin\{0,1,3,-3\}}}
\sum_{a<b}s_as_b.
\]
For any two distinct branch points \(\alpha,\beta\),
\[
\sum_x\chi((x-\alpha)(x-\beta))=-1,
\]
so the total over all six pairs is \(-6\). The branch-point contributions are:

\[
x=0:1+2\delta,\qquad
x=1:3,\qquad
x=3:1+2\delta,\qquad
x=-3:1+2\delta.
\]
Thus
\[
E=-6-(6+6\delta)=-12-6\delta.
\]
For a non-branch point, the pairwise sum is \(6\) if all four signs agree, \(-2\) if exactly two are \(+1\), and \(0\) otherwise. Hence
\[
6A-2B=-12-6\delta,
\]
or
\[
3A-B=-6-3\delta.
\]

It remains to evaluate \(Q_p\). Use the Möbius change
\[
t=\frac{2x}{x-3},\qquad x=\frac{3t}{t-2}.
\]
Then
\[
x(x-1)(x-3)(x+3)
=
\frac{216\,t(t^2-1)}{(t-2)^4}.
\]
Since \(p\equiv1\pmod8\), \(\chi(2)=1\), so
\[
\chi(216)=\chi(3)=\delta.
\]
The map \(x\neq3\leftrightarrow t\neq2\) is bijective, and \(x=3\) contributes \(0\). Therefore
\[
Q_p
=\delta\sum_{t\neq2}\chi(t^3-t)
=\delta\left(\sum_t\chi(t^3-t)-\chi(6)\right).
\]
Now \(\chi(6)=\delta\). For
\[
E_0:y^2=t^3-t,
\]
the CM trace calculation for \(p\equiv1\pmod8\), with
\[
p=u^2+v^2,\qquad u\equiv1\pmod4,
\]
gives
\[
\sum_t\chi(t^3-t)=-2u.
\]
Thus
\[
Q_p=\delta(-2u-\delta)=-2\delta u-1.
\]

Now solve
\[
A+B=\frac{p-4+Q_p}{2}
=\frac{p-5-2\delta u}{2},
\]
and
\[
3A-B=-6-3\delta.
\]
This gives
\[
A=\frac{p-17-6\delta-2\delta u}{8},
\qquad
B=\frac{3p-3+6\delta-6\delta u}{8}.
\]

\[
\boxed{
\bigl(A(p),B(p)\bigr)
=
\left(
\frac{p-17-6\delta-2\delta u}{8},
\frac{3p-3+6\delta-6\delta u}{8}
\right)
}
\]
